```{r}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Put your input file in variable DATA 
DATA <- "example_script_PSrates.xlsx"


#2. Parameters for plot
#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Points color
COLOUR <- "#000000"

# Select a palette for CI color
PALETTE <- "Greens"

#3. Global parameters
var1 <- "Line"
var2 <- "Treatment"
MEASURE_COL <- "PSIIrate"

```

## 1. Introduction

The analysis reported here is part of the manuscript Romand et al. 2021. The script performs statistical analysis on data grouped by `r var1` and `r var2` and plots a graph. Different approaches are used depending on the normality of the data as determined by the Shapiro test. If data follow a normal distribution, then the script performs Anova and post-hoc Tukey tests and draws a plot with confidence interval centered on mean. If data do not follow a normal distribution then a Kruskal-Wallis and a pot-hoc Dunn test are performed. The same plot is drawn using the medians and boostrap calculated 95% confidence intervals. The plots are also saved as pdf and vector (SVG) files.


## 2. Data

A 3 column data set in `xlsx`. Column 1, `r var2`; column 2, `r var1` and column 3 the measured quantity, in this case `r MEASURE_COL`. 
The 2 first columns are factors that are used to group the data.

This script can be simply modified to analyse different parameters or different Treatments. It can also be modified to analyse data grouped by additional factors such as Time.

#### Functions used in the script

```{r}
#===============================================================================
# Draw the bar plot if data follow a normal distribution
#===============================================================================

plot_normal <- function(df, my_colours, my_summary) {
  p <- ggplot(data = my_summary, aes(x = !!sym(var1), y = !!sym(MEASURE_COL), fill = !!sym(var1))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(), width = 0.8, color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = !!sym(MEASURE_COL) - ci, ymax = !!sym(MEASURE_COL) + ci), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_quasirandom(data = df, aes(x = !!sym(var1), y = !!sym(MEASURE_COL)), color = COLOUR, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_colours) +
    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", var2)), strip.position = "bottom", scales = "free_x") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
  print(p)
}

#===============================================================================
# Draw the bar plot if data do not follow a normal distribution
#===============================================================================

plot_not_normal <- function(df, my_colours, booted_summary) {
  p <- ggplot(data = booted_summary, aes(x = !!sym(var1), y = !!sym(MEASURE_COL), fill = !!sym(var1))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(), width = 0.8, color = "darkgrey") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower_ci_perc, ymax = upper_ci_perc), width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.8)) +
    geom_quasirandom(data = df, aes(x = !!sym(var1), y = !!sym(MEASURE_COL)), color = COLOUR, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = my_colours) +
    facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", var2)), strip.position = "bottom", scales = "free_x") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
  print(p)
}

#===============================================================================
# Check normality of the data. Exit the loop if one set of data doesn't follow a 
# normal distribution.
# Return TRUE if all data follow a normal distribution
#===============================================================================

check_normality <- function(shapiro_df) {
    # Data are supposed to follow normal distribution
    flag_normal <- TRUE
    
    for (i in 1 : nrow(shapiro_df)) {
        # Check if the p-value is not NA and greater than 0.05
        if (!is.na(shapiro_df[i, 4]) && shapiro_df[i, 4] > 0.05) {
            # Do nothing, this data set follows a normal distribution
        } else if (!is.na(shapiro_df[i, 4]) && shapiro_df[i, 4] <= 0.05) {
            # If p-value is less than or equal to 0.05, mark it as non-normal
            flag_normal <- FALSE
            break
        }
        # If p-value is NA, we skip the check and treat it as normal
    }
    return(flag_normal)
}

#===============================================================================
# Check variance homogeneity of the data using Levene's test
# Return TRUE if all subsets have homogeneous variance
#===============================================================================

check_variance <- function(levene_df) {
    # Data are supposed to have homogeneous variance
    flag_homogeneous <- TRUE
    
    for (i in 1 : nrow(levene_df)) {
        if(levene_df[i, "p.value"] > 0.05) {
            # Variance is homogeneous
        } else {
            # Variance is not homogeneous
            flag_homogeneous <- FALSE
            break
        }
    }
    return(flag_homogeneous)
}

#===============================================================================
#Function to calculate the median (for bootstrapping)
#===============================================================================

samplemedian <- function(d, i) {
    median(d[i])
}

#===============================================================================
#Function for Dunn test
#===============================================================================

test_dunn <- function() {
    pval <- as.data.frame(df %>% group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>% dunn_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"))
    print(df %>% group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>% dunn_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), p.adjust.method = "bonferroni"))
    return(pval)
}
```

#### Main script

```{r fig.show='hide',  message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = 'hide', echo=TRUE, fig.retina = 1}
# Import Data
df <- read_excel(DATA)
df[[var1]] <- make.names(df[[var1]])

# Define color
my_colours = brewer.pal(n = 9, PALETTE)[9:3]

# Determining data normality status
shapiro_df <- df %>%
  group_by(!!sym(var2), !!sym(var1)) %>%
  summarise(
    statistic = if(length(unique(.data[[MEASURE_COL]])) > 1) {
      shapiro.test(.data[[MEASURE_COL]])$statistic
    } else {
      NA  # Assign NA or a custom message for groups with identical values
    },
    p.value = if(length(unique(.data[[MEASURE_COL]])) > 1) {
      shapiro.test(.data[[MEASURE_COL]])$p.value
    } else {
      NA  # Assign NA or a custom message for groups with identical values
    }
  )

# After the summarise pipe, call the check_normality function separately
flag_normal <- check_normality(shapiro_df)

# Determining variance homogeneity status using Levene's test
levene_df <- df %>%
  group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>%
  do({
    data_subset <- .
    if (n_distinct(data_subset[[var1]]) > 1) {
      # Try running leveneTest and handle cases where it fails gracefully
      tryCatch({
        levene_result <- leveneTest(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), data = data_subset)
        data.frame(statistic = as.numeric(levene_result$`F value`[1]), p.value = as.numeric(levene_result$`Pr(>F)`[1]))
      }, error = function(e) {
        # If there is an error, return NA for statistic and p-value
        data.frame(statistic = NA, p.value = NA)
      })
    } else {
      # If there's only one level, return NA
      data.frame(statistic = NA, p.value = NA)
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup()



# Check variance homogeneity status
flag_homogeneous <- check_variance(levene_df)


# Data treatement according to normality status
if(flag_normal == TRUE) {
    #print("Data follow a normal distribution")
    
    # Summary
    my_summary <- summarySE(df, measurevar=MEASURE_COL, groupvars=c(var1, var2))
    
    # Plot
    plot_normal(df, my_colours, my_summary)
    
    # Stats
    anova_results <- df %>% group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>%  anova_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)))
    
    # Perform Tukey HSD test
tukey_results <- df %>%
  group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>%
  tukey_hsd(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)))

# Check Tukey results to ensure valid p-values
print(tukey_results)

# Fit the linear model
model <- lm(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), data = df)

# Obtain estimated marginal means
emm <- emmeans(model, as.formula(paste("~", var1)))

# Generate CLD letters
cld_result <- cld(emm, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, sort = FALSE)

# Create the final CLD table
cld_table <- cld_result %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::select(!!sym(var1), cld = .group)

# Print the final CLD table
print(cld_table)
    
   # Save plot
    ggsave("my_ggplot1.pdf", width=4, height=5)
    ggsave("my_ggplot1.svg", width=4, height=5)
    
} else {
    #print("Data do not follow a normal distribution")
    
    # Calculate Median and 95%CI by bootstrap (Largely based on code by Peter Kamerman: 
    #https://www.painblogr.org/2017-10-18-purrring-through-bootstraps.html)
    
    #1. Set the seed
    set.seed(12345)
    
    #2. Create nested datafile to allow boostrapping on each subgroup.
    my_data_nested <- df %>% group_by(!!sym(var1), !!sym(var2)) %>% nest()
    
    #3. Add boostrapped median values to my_nested_data
    my_data_nested %<>% dplyr::mutate(booted = purrr::map(.x = data, ~ boot::boot(data = .x[[MEASURE_COL]],statistic = samplemedian, R = 10000, stype = "i")))
    
    #4. Check if the bootstrap object contains valid values before plotting
    plots <- purrr::map(.x = my_data_nested$booted, ~ {
      if (all(is.finite(.x$t))) {
        tryCatch({
          plot(.x)
        }, error = function(e) {
          warning("Error in plotting bootstrap results: ", conditionMessage(e))
          NULL
        })
      } else {
        warning("Bootstrap results contain NA/NaN values, skipping plot.")
        NULL
      }
    })
    print(plots)


    #5. Add boostrapped 95%CI around median values to my_nested_data, 
    #95%CI determined based on "perc" & "bca"
    my_data_nested %<>% mutate(booted_ci = purrr::map(.x = booted, 
                                                      ~ tryCatch({
                                                        boot::boot.ci(.x, conf = 0.95, type = c("perc", "bca"))
                                                      }, error = function(e) {
                                                        warning("Error in calculating confidence intervals: ", conditionMessage(e))
                                                        NULL
                                                      })))
    
    #6. Table of each <S3: bootci> object to check
    ci_table <-purrr::map(.x = my_data_nested$booted_ci, ~ print(.x))
    
    # 7. Get the stats (median and 95% CI) from the nested dataframe into a regular dataframe 
# (my_data_booted_summary) with 95%CI determined by "bca" or "perc" method
booted_summary <- my_data_nested %>% 
  mutate(
    !!sym(MEASURE_COL) := purrr::map_dbl(.x = booted_ci, ~ if (!is.null(.x)) .x$t0 else NA_real_),
    lower_ci_bca = purrr::map_dbl(.x = booted_ci, ~ if (!is.null(.x) && "bca" %in% names(.x)) .x$bca[[4]] else NA_real_),
    upper_ci_bca = purrr::map_dbl(.x = booted_ci, ~ if (!is.null(.x) && "bca" %in% names(.x)) .x$bca[[5]] else NA_real_),
    lower_ci_perc = purrr::map_dbl(.x = booted_ci, ~ if (!is.null(.x) && "perc" %in% names(.x)) .x$perc[[4]] else NA_real_),
    upper_ci_perc = purrr::map_dbl(.x = booted_ci, ~ if (!is.null(.x) && "perc" %in% names(.x)) .x$perc[[5]] else NA_real_)
  ) %>%  
  dplyr::select(-data, -booted, -booted_ci)

# Update missing error bars in booted_summary
booted_summary <- booted_summary %>% 
  mutate(
    lower_ci_perc = ifelse(is.na(lower_ci_perc), lower_ci_bca, lower_ci_perc),
    upper_ci_perc = ifelse(is.na(upper_ci_perc), upper_ci_bca, upper_ci_perc)
  )
    # Plot
    plot_not_normal(df, my_colours, booted_summary)
    
    # Stats
     
    kruskal_pval <- (df %>% group_by(!!sym(var2))%>%kruskal_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)))) %>% dplyr::select(!!sym(var2), p)
    
    kruskal_pval <- as.data.frame(kruskal_pval)
    
    print(kruskal_pval)
    
    pval_dunn <- df %>% group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>%   dunn_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), p.adjust.method = "BY")


# Perform Dunn's test with BY adjustment
pval_dunn <- df %>% 
  group_by(!!sym(var2)) %>% 
  dunn_test(as.formula(paste(MEASURE_COL, "~", var1)), p.adjust.method = "BY")

# Extract all unique lines
unique_lines <- unique(c(pval_dunn$group1, pval_dunn$group2))

# Create a matrix to represent significance relationships between groups
# Initialize it to TRUE, which means all groups are significantly different by default
comparison_matrix <- matrix(TRUE, nrow = length(unique_lines), ncol = length(unique_lines))
rownames(comparison_matrix) <- unique_lines
colnames(comparison_matrix) <- unique_lines

# Set non-significant comparisons (p.adj > 0.05) to FALSE in the matrix
for (i in 1:nrow(pval_dunn)) {
  if (pval_dunn$p.adj[i] > 0.05) {
    g1 <- pval_dunn$group1[i]
    g2 <- pval_dunn$group2[i]
    comparison_matrix[g1, g2] <- FALSE
    comparison_matrix[g2, g1] <- FALSE
  }
}

# Use multcompView::multcompLetters to generate the CLD letters
group_letters <- multcompView::multcompLetters(comparison_matrix)$Letters

# Convert the letters to a data frame
cld_table <- data.frame(Line = names(group_letters), cld = group_letters)

# Display the CLD table
print(cld_table)

    
    # Save plot
    ggsave("my_ggplot1.pdf", width=4, height=5)
    ggsave("my_ggplot1.svg", width=4, height=5)
}

```

##### Summary statistics

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
  kable(my_summary, caption = "Table 3: Summary statistics for normal data", digits = 3)%>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", "hover")
} else {
  kable(booted_summary, caption = "Table 3: Summary statistics for non-normal data", digits = 3)%>%
```

##### Statistical tests within each Treatment condition

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}

  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", "hover")
} else {
# Kruskal results table
  kable(kruskal_pval, caption = "Table 4: Kruskal-Wallis test results", digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "striped", "hover")
}
```

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}

}
```
